description: Merge-and-shrink builds an *abstraction* of a planning task: a smaller transition system that maps groups of real states to one abstract state. It starts with one small transition system (a *factor*) per state variable. Then it repeatedly picks two factors, *shrinks* them by merging equivalent abstract states until their product fits a size limit, and *merges* them into their synchronized product. The goal distances in the last factor never overestimate the true cost (they are *admissible*), so A* with this heuristic finds cheapest plans. With exact bisimulation shrinking and no size limit, the heuristic is perfect on tasks without conditional effects and derived variables.

papers.authors: Malte Helmert, Patrik Haslum, Jörg Hoffmann, Raz Nissim
papers.title: Merge-and-Shrink Abstraction: A Method for Generating Lower Bounds in Factored State Spaces
Merge-and-Shrink: A Compositional Theory of Transformations of Factored Transition Systems
